rootCauses.cause: Filter flags rules that only touch the company indirectly: supplier or grower inputs, mixed-scope rules whose relevant part targets other entities, and rules that bind only the agency. It treats 'mentions something we buy or do' as an obligation.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Add one exclusion to the 'strict' prompt set: 'Not relevant if the obligation falls on suppliers, growers, labs, covered entities or the agency itself, or if only an optional or unrelated section touches the company. Relevant only if the company itself must do or change something.' This targets the shared pattern in all four llmReasons, where the duty sits with someone else or with the agency.
rootCauses.risk: Recall loss on genuinely indirect-but-binding rules, such as supplier rules the company must contractually pass through. It could also make the filter even more dismissive of borderline direct rules like the power-bank NPRM.

rootCauses.cause: Debatable key: HHS drug-testing guidelines (urine and oral fluid) underpin DOT/FAA-mandated testing for airline safety-sensitive staff, and the TCPA consent-revocation rule governs pharmacy reminder calls and texts. These are plausibly real obligations that the key leaves unlabeled. Judge P(relevant) ran 0.53–0.54 for the HHS documents.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Run a key review on these three documents and either label them relevant (indirect or compliance) or mark them 'acceptable either way' so extras on them are not scored as false positives.
rootCauses.risk: Loosening the key could hide real over-flagging. Keep the reviewed items explicitly tagged so the precision trend stays comparable across runs.

rootCauses.cause: Action writer produces generic or speculative actions without the rule's substance. It omits the payment cap and the direction of quota changes, and invents 'tightening' of ADHD supply when quotas were raised. It apparently works from the title and relevance reason only, not from the rule text.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Pass the document abstract/summary excerpt into the action-generation prompt. Require the action to state (a) what changed and in which direction and (b) whether anything is required of the company, and forbid speculation beyond the excerpt. Dates stay excluded.
rootCauses.risk: Longer actions may fail the 'clear' judge. More source text also invites the model to copy dates or legal jargon into the action, so the no-date check must stay enforced.

rootCauses.cause: Filter rejects a real proposed rule because it is 'only a proposal'. The strict prompt's exclusions are being read as excluding NPRMs, even when the proposal would impose operational duties (power-bank limits) the airline must enforce.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Add to the 'strict' prompt set: 'Proposed rules that would impose duties on the company's own operations are relevant (comment/prepare); do not reject solely because a rule is proposed.'
rootCauses.risk: More extra flags on NPRMs with speculative impact, partially offsetting the precision gain from the first fix.

rootCauses.cause: Verified effective date was found but not shown. The headline-date code appears to suppress dates for docType Notice or Low tier, even though a verified 'effective' date exists (the final order is effective 2026-11-10).
rootCauses.proposedChange: In the date-display code, show the verified effective/compliance date whenever one was found, regardless of docType or tier.
rootCauses.risk: Notices that carry several dates (comment deadline, meeting, effective) might headline the wrong one. Keep the kind label ('effective') next to the date.

rootCauses.cause: Relevance decision contradicts its own reason. The LLM wrote 'creates no obligation, so not relevant' but the document was flagged, which points to output-parsing or decision-field mismatch.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Require a structured boolean 'relevant' field emitted before the reason, and add a code check that rejects or reruns outputs whose reason says 'not relevant' while the flag is true.
rootCauses.risk: Minimal. Reruns add latency and cost, and an overly aggressive text check could misfire on reasons that say 'not relevant except…'.

rootCauses.cause: Clarity rubric penalizes a correct 'no action needed' recommendation as lacking a concrete next step. For a no-obligation document, 'take no action' is the right advice. This failure only appears because of the spurious flag on the same document.
rootCauses.proposedChange: Amend the 'clear' judge instruction: 'An explicit no-action recommendation with a plain reason counts as a concrete next step.'
rootCauses.risk: Could let lazy 'no action' outputs pass on documents that do require action. That case should still be caught by the relevance and covers signals.
